messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] running knitr D3 example via RStudio
parts:
Hi Herman,

As you have noticed, you only need to include d3.js in your document:

<script src="http://d3js.org/d3.v2.min.js"></script>

Putting this line after line #10 in the Rmd file should work.

You did not see d3.js in Rmd because it was actually included by the
Jekyll template:
https://github.com/supstat/vistat/blob/gh-pages/_includes/themes/dinky/default.html#L22-L24
When you are not working with Jekyll, you need to manually include D3.

Regards,
Yihui

On Sat, Mar 16, 2013 at 2:20 PM, Herman Sontrop
<herman....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> my question basically boils down to how to compile the knitr D3 example via
> RStudio?
>
> The example can be found at http://yihui.name/knitr/demo/javascript/ while a
> rendered version can be seen at
> http://vis.supstat.com/2012/11/contour-plots-with-d3-and-r/
>
> When I process the corresponding .rmd file
> (https://github.com/supstat/vistat/blob/gh-pages/_source/2012-11-07-contour-plots-with-d3-and-r.Rmd)
> in RStudio (via knitHTML) all seems to work well. However, when I run the
> resulting HTML output file generated by knitr in a browser (Firefox, Chrome)
> I see all but the D3 part of the example :-(
>
> For instance, in the head of the generated HTML (see attach example.html)
> no D3 library reference is inserted (something like '<script
> src="http://d3js.org/d3.v2.min.js"></script>') so I guess therefore the
> browser does not know what to do with the D3 part.
>
> I am aware of previous posts
> (https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/knitr/mHrG0N2SdWE),
> however, these seem not mention a problem compiling the document.
>
> If someone knows an answer it would be a great help!
>
> kind regards, Herman
